GenAI - Code - Orchestrators - KiloCode: /model – Opens an inline menu to inspect, list, or switch the current AI LLM model brain handling your prompts.
/mode – Swaps agent behavioral modes instantly (e.g., /mode architect or /mode code).
/reload – Forces Kilo to instantly re-scan your project files and pull in any updated custom project configuration rules.
/auto-approve – Toggles automatic execution permissions on or off for filesystem read/write steps.
/privacy – Toggles data privacy protection, which dynamically blurs out recognizable PII inside the terminal panel.
/exit (or /quit / /q) – Terminates the active Kilo instance cleanly and returns you to your standard terminal shell.
kilo mcp add <name> <command> – Configures an external Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to extend the agent's skills.
kilo mcp list – Lists all currently active and connected MCP server integrations.
kilo db path – Prints the absolute file path to the internal SQLite database where your local chats are saved.
kilo upgrade – Automatically checks for updates and installs the latest stable production release binary.
• kilo uninstall – Orderly removes the Kilo framework layout from your global system pathways.
kilo auth login – Opens an authentication wizard to securely link your Kilo account or cloud provider credentials.
kilo auth list – Displays an overview of your currently configured AI providers and validation access status.
kilo models [provider] – Lists all AI models available to your current global endpoint configuration.
• kilo stats – Tracks and displays token consumption metrics, local tool calls, and overall execution costs.
--continue (or -c) – Instantly resumes your very last active session without needing an ID
--session <id> – Directs Kilo to reload and resume a specific historical conversation thread.
--mode <architect|ask|code|debug> – Forces the agent into a specific behavior (e.g., planning vs. raw file editing).
--model <name> (or -m) – Sets a specific model explicitly for the runtime cycle (e.g., anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet).
--auto – Autonomous mode. The agent executes files edits without prompting you for safety confirmation alerts.
• --file <path> (or -f) – Explicitly attaches targeted codebase files straight into the initial chat context window.

• Isolated Project Rules: You can put a kilo.jsonc, AGENTS.md, or a .kilocodeignore file inside Folder_A and a completely different set of rules inside Folder_B. They will never conflict or bleed into each other.

• Isolated Chat Histories: Kilo Code tracks your project roots by their absolute file path. When you run kilo session list inside ~/projects/app-one, it will only show the chat histories for that specific application. If you move over to ~/projects/app-two, it will show a completely separate history.
kilo – Launches the interactive terminal user interface (TUI) coding session in your current working directory.
kilo session list – Displays a historical table of recent chat sessions, timestamps, and their unique Session IDs.
kilo session delete <session_id> – Permanently deletes a specific session from your local history database.
kilo export <session_id> – Exports a raw JSON payload of all events, tool calls, and structural history for that session.
• kilo import <file_path_or_url> – Imports a saved JSON session snapshot or data pulled from a web sharing link.
/sessions (or /resume / /continue) – Lists your history and lets you hot-swap to another conversation thread mid-session.
/new (or /clear) – Wipes the active conversation buffer and spins up a brand new, isolated session in the folder.
/fork – Splits your timeline from a designated message block to try out a different development path safely.
/undo – Reverts the last prompt submission and rolls back any file or code changes the AI just made.
/redo – Re-applies a previously undone prompt or code modification step.
• /compact (or /summarize) – Compresses older messages in the chat into summaries to save your prompt tokens.

It looks at your prompt and immediately assumes you want it to modify, delete, or create actual source files in your codebase. It skips high-level architectural debates or planning documentation and goes straight to editing. • It automatically triggers its internal tools to read your file tree, patch lines of code, and execute terminal test commands to verify its changes.
kilo run 'your instruction' – One-shot execution mode. It processes a single instruction directly from your shell and exits.

In Architect Mode, Kilo is structurally blocked from writing raw application code immediately. Instead, it shifts its entire focus to analyzing your requirements, mapping file dependencies, and outputting technical blueprints.
Once your workspace is configured, your daily routine moves away from loose conversational prompts and follows a rigid, step-by-step command pipeline:
Write the Spec: You manually define your requirements or features inside SPECIFICATION.md.
Generate the Architectural Plan: Run Kilo and instruct it to build a technical blueprint based on your spec:
Generate the Implementation Tasks: Force the agent to break down the approved blueprint into a strict checklist:
Autonomous Execution: Switch Kilo into Code Mode to execute the task list sequentially using its autonomous capabilities:

Kilo Memory lets Kilo remember useful details about a project across sessions, so you do not have to repeat decisions, constraints, environment setup, or corrections. It is opt-in and scoped to one project.
/export – Generates and saves a clean Markdown .md text transcript file of your entire active conversation locally.
/copy – Copies the exact plain text block of the most recent AI response to your system clipboard.
/share – Generates a shareable cloud URL snapshot link to securely show your session history to others.
• /diff – Spawns an interactive side-by-side terminal diff viewer showing every edit the agent has currently staged.
